cloud-image-layers.description: Produce the layers an image project declares in image-layers.json, byte-deterministically: tarballs get fixed epoch mtimes, sorted entries, numeric root ownership and explicit modes, and an image-owned tool layer is cross-compiled with the pinned Go toolchain under -trimpath, so the same inputs hash to the same layer on any host, and a tool the @putnami/go artifact already ships for linux/amd64 is restored from that verified store instead. Nothing becomes a layer unverified — a downloaded artifact is checked against its publisher's checksum or the workspace lock's integrity, and a compiled or restored tool against its own embedded build info (module version, main package and toolchain, read without executing it). Run it before `putnami package`: the image project's content key is a hash of these bytes, and --check (the package-verb precondition) refuses a set the workspace no longer describes.

project.description: Image project directory (default: the resolved project root).

check.description: Verify an already-produced layer set instead of producing one: every declared layer has a record, its file still hashes to what that record claims, and its identity is the one this checkout declares today — the whole set of inputs that select the artifact (a tool's module/version/package, an image's repository, rendered tag and pinned digest, the CLI's version and lock integrity), not the version alone. Reads only.

cache-provider.description: Run as the remote build-cache provider over the JSONL provider RPC (machine protocol; launched once per build run by the scheduler, not for interactive use). The explicit task identity selects this provider; command-name and extension-version capability probes are not used.

credential-provider.description: Run as the engine's registry credential provider over the protocol/registry credential-provider JSONL RPC (machine protocol; launched by the engine when --providers install enables the read purpose, not for interactive use). On a hosted run the read credential comes from the run's Delivery install capability under the run credential; on a developer machine it is one short-lived registry bearer for the signed-in user of a linked checkout. The publish purpose answers absence.

session-reporter.description: Run as the engine's session reporter over the protocol/cli session-reporting JSONL wire (machine protocol; launched by the engine when PUTNAMI_SESSION_REPORTER selects @putnami/cloud, not for interactive use). Each frame is one POST of the original session.json / events.jsonl bytes to the Delivery run-session ingest under the run credential.

log-reporter.description: Run as the engine's log reporter over the protocol/cli session-reporting JSONL wire (machine protocol; launched by the engine when PUTNAMI_LOG_REPORTER selects @putnami/cloud, not for interactive use). Each frame is one POST of events.jsonl bytes to the Delivery run-log ingest under the run credential, while tasks run.

workspace-install.description: Replay declared local wiring and caches for a linked workspace, offline and without changing the session. An unlinked workspace is a successful skip; never creates, links, subscribes or activates.

build.description: Materialize an image project's declared generated layers as ordinary build outputs. This keeps a cold monorepo CI run self-bootstrapping: build --impacted produces the runner bytes before the trusted post-gate stage packages and publishes the runner-backed worker from the same checkout. The package contribution still re-verifies the exact bytes and current pins immediately before assembly.

validate.description: Validate existing authored production Config inputs and declared site-content source metadata without packaging.

package.description: Verify declared image layers when present, build a canonical secret-free Config member for schema-bearing projects, and assemble the site-content bundles of a docs site project (activated by a section landing page, <section>/index.md). Every package step is local and produces immutable inputs for the selected release-set publication.

env.description: Environment to package; native Config members currently support prod only.

namespace.description: Explicit intended Put namespace for native Config publication.

test.description: Run a project's committed shell test harness (tests/run.sh). Activation is the harness file itself, so this only ever schedules for a project that HAS one, such as an image whose subject under test is a bash entrypoint and therefore has no language extension to provide `test`. Exit status is the verdict.

publish.description: Publish Putnami Cloud config schema, environment values, migration bundles, a workload's deployment declaration, immutable archives, and the site-content bundles of a docs project. Archive, deployment and site-content publication emit a native release-set member only after Put accepts or byte-confirms the exact manifest.

cloud-deploy.description: `deploy status <release-id>` shows one release and the state of each workload; it exits 1 when the release failed or ended partial. `deploy publish-v2 --request-file <path>` submits a release set to one environment as an operator continuous-delivery request; a rollback names an older release set.

wait.description: Block until every workload of the release settles or --timeout fires.

cloud-status.description: Show one line per entry that has a status (whoami, token, registries, packages, channels, ci, cache, source, config, secrets, db, env): ok, degraded, failing or unknown, with the command that shows more. Exits 1 when an entry is failing; --strict also fails on degraded and unknown (supports --output). `putnami cloud <entry> status` shows one entry with its metrics; `putnami cloud env status --health` prints the deployment table.

cloud-env.description: Environments: `env status [<env>]` compares what putnami.ci.json declares with what runs, per environment and workload (--health and --provenance print the deployment table); `env doctor [<env>]` checks each continuous-delivery prerequisite and prints the fix for every row that is not ok. Both exit 1 when a row is failing; --strict also fails on degraded and unknown; `env enable [<env>]` applies every workspace-owned fix (supports --output).

cloud-packages.description: Manage package namespaces, grants, mirrors, OCI image moves and archive publication.

cloud-registry-token.description: Mint your registry bearer for one known registry host.

cloud-oci.description: Copy or retag images on the Putnami OCI registry server-side.

cloud-cache.description: Show or disable the remote build cache config.

cloud-report.description: Submit a delivery run conclusion for the current pushed commit.

cloud-track.description: Change a workspace producer track and optional runner channel atomically.

cloud-channels.description: Set, show or follow release channels.

cloud-ci.description: Operate workspace CI runs and recovery.

cloud-image-layers.description: Produce the project's declared image layers under .gen/layers (normalized tarballs plus a checksum sidecar). Uncached on purpose: the producer downloads upstream artifacts and writes into the project's own .gen, and a cross-worktree cache hit would serve one checkout's layer bytes to another.

cloud-image-layers-check.description: Verify the project's produced layers against image-layers.json and the workspace sources that derive their versions: every declared layer has a record, its produced file still hashes to what that record claims, and its version is the one the workspace declares today. Reads only — no network, no registry, no execution. Uncached on purpose: it exists to observe the CURRENT state of a .gen tree the producer writes outside any cache key, so a hit would report a verdict about bytes this checkout may no longer have.

cloud-shell-test.description: Execute the project's committed shell test harness at tests/run.sh; its exit status is the verdict. Uncached on purpose: the harness drives real git and process fixtures, so its inputs are wider than any declarable file set and a stale hit would report a green gate for an unexercised entrypoint. The limit is 900 s because the harness runs a cold `putnami test` of the libs it covers.

cloud-cache-provider.description: Remote build-cache provider RPC server: reads/writes provider-RPC JSONL on stdin/stdout. Started by its explicit provider task identity, not command-name or extension-version feature detection.

cloud-credential-provider.description: Registry credential provider: reads protocol/registry credential-provider JSONL on stdin and writes one answer per request on stdout. A read credential on a hosted run is a POST to ${PUTNAMI_CLOUD_INGEST_URL}/capabilities/install under the run credential the engine sends at initialize; on a developer machine it is minted for the signed-in user. Started by the engine's reserved credential-provider discovery as the extension's native runtime.

cloud-session-reporter.description: Session reporter provider: reads protocol/cli SessionReportingChunk JSONL on stdin, POSTs each frame to ${PUTNAMI_CLOUD_INGEST_URL}/sessions under the run credential, and writes one SessionReportingAck per frame on stdout. A hosted run hands the run credential over the session reporting protocol 2 handshake (initialize, then authenticate) before the first chunk; otherwise it is PUTNAMI_SESSION_REPORTER_TOKEN. Started by the engine's reserved session-reporter discovery on the explicitly selected extension.

cloud-log-reporter.description: Log reporter provider: reads protocol/cli SessionReportingChunk JSONL on stdin, POSTs each events.jsonl frame to ${PUTNAMI_CLOUD_INGEST_URL}/logs under the run credential with its sequence, offset and digest, and writes one SessionReportingAck per frame on stdout. A hosted run hands the run credential over the session reporting protocol 2 handshake (initialize, then authenticate) before the first chunk; otherwise it is PUTNAMI_LOG_REPORTER_TOKEN. Started by the engine's reserved log-reporter discovery on the explicitly selected extension.

cloud-install.description: Replay declared local wiring and caches for a linked workspace, offline and without changing the session. An unlinked workspace is a successful skip; never creates, links, subscribes or activates.

cloud-db.description: Request/list/revoke ephemeral database access grants and open a localhost psql bridge over the db-gateway.

cloud-validate-site-content.description: Inspect declared site sections, mounts, regular-file policy and paths using fresh directory metadata; never read or hash payloads, generate artifacts or assemble archives. Uncached: it checks directory metadata (empty section directories, symlink vs regular file) that the file hasher does not key.

cloud-validate-config-project.description: Validate the declared native Config member from existing local artifacts; skip projects without a Config namespace. Cached on the files and parameters the extension README lists; refuses --schema-from and any project other than the one in its working directory.

cloud-validate-config.description: Validate an authored Config member from existing local artifacts only; writes no package artifact and performs no network request.

cloud-source.description: Connect, inspect, or disconnect a workspace GitHub repository.

cloud-publish-config.description: Publish app schema + per-env config values.

cloud-package-config-member.description: Build the canonical secret-free production Config member consumed by native publication. Uncached: the member embeds the full HEAD commit, the origin repository and the linked workspace id, and is written outside the project under .putnami/out.

cloud-publish-migration.description: Publish a workload's migration bundle to the Put registry.

cloud-publish-config-project.description: Publish selected project schema + per-env config values.

cloud-publish-migration-project.description: Send the selected project's migration bundle to Data when one was built; an existing bundle requires an explicit project namespace.

cloud-publish-archives.description: Publish a workload's pre-built archives to the Put registry.

cloud-package-site-content.description: Assemble and contract-verify every section bundle of a site project, with no network. Its task identity keys on the project tree and is the selection fingerprint of the project's site-content members. Uncached: bundle.json embeds the short HEAD commit and the task identity is the release selection fingerprint.

cloud-publish-site-content-project.description: Publish exactly the site-content members the release-set plan selected for this site project, at the planned version, moving the plan's first channel in the same atomic Put publish.

cloud-publish-deployment-project.description: Publish exactly the deployment member the release-set plan selected for this workload: the canonical <project>/.gen/deployment.json its language package step wrote, byte for byte, at the planned version. A selected member whose declaration is missing or invalid fails the step; without a selected member the step publishes nothing.

cloud-publish-archives-project.description: Publish the selected project's pre-built archives to the Put registry when present.

cloud-deploy.description: Show one release, or submit a release set with `deploy publish-v2`. The budget covers a whole release set, optionally awaited with --wait --timeout, not a single project.

cloud-status.description: Summarize the workspace: one line per entry with its state and the command that shows more.

cloud-env.description: Check or converge one environment's continuous-delivery prerequisites.

cloud-logs.description: Query or follow a workspace app's logs.

cloud-metrics.description: Query a workspace app's metric series.
